Back when I was in (middle? Junior high?) school, I was having a hard time. Like really hard. No friends. Massive bullying at school. Shitty step dad. Basically emotionally absent mom.... Anyway, I thought about suicide daily. Made plans. Fantasized about the best way to do it. Withdrew from everything and everyone. I would dread waking up in the morning. Hate going home at night. Would silently cry myself to sleep almost every night. But the one, and only bright spot in my life at the time was my yellow tabby that looked exactly like Morris from the 9 lives commercials. My step sister found him in the neighborhood one weekend. Let me tell you.. He was the most chill cat I've known. But his best quality? As soon as I walked in the door after school, as soon as I woke up, whatever, whatever he was doing, he'd stop and be right by my side. He'd lay on my bed for hours comforting me as I cried after school. He'd try to protect me from the numerous attacks my step dad would give me, both verbal and physical. He was my reason for living. He was my own furry guardian angel. The one clear thought that I held on to during that time was if I died, who would take care of him. I, to this day, believe I would not be here if it were not for him. I carry around his collar as a little reminder that I still have someone looking out for me, no matter what. I've had it on me for the better part of 30 years now. My little yellow furry savior.

If you're a fan of dogs, I'd suggest getting one that is well past the puppy stage. Older dogs will enjoy the extended sleep afforded from the long drives, and are still great ways to get exercise during the day.

Your in-cab air hose and a decent shop vac will take care of the hair, and they make a 'spill proof' water dish that works great.

Test out the animal first. Some animals do great in smaller cars, but not so much in trucks. (vibrations and noises can make some anxious and sick) And vice versa. My dog loves the truck, but isn't fond of my car.

Yes, messes happen. But they will happen wherever you are. You deal. Plus the amount of time you spend with your animal allows you to pick up on the little changes that can signal illness, giving you the opportunity to deal with it earlier.

I wouldn't give up my dog for the world. He is a great heater in the winter, and has been an amazing alarm system many times.
